result.summary:
WF-03 Step 3c -- REVIEWER RE-GATE of the ISS-0200 edit after rework iteration 1. PASS.

PLAIN VERDICT: PASS. The BLOCKER raised at 03b is remedied. All five gated items clear. Nothing that passed at 03b was disturbed. Three MINORs below are for filing, not for rework -- but MINOR-C-1 and MINOR-C-2 are actionable BEFORE Step 5 dispatches, and ORCH should carry them into that dispatch rather than only file them.

I re-gated only what 03b's next_action scoped and what this dispatch named. I did not reopen the NO-CHANGE verdict, the NOT-A-RULE framing, the single declaration of 6,000, (B)(ii)/(C), `no_defect`'s bar or name, or the sha-recording mechanism. AC4 I re-derived, as instructed, because a rework is when a protected span gets clipped.

=== (1) THE BLOCKER'S REMEDY: PASS ===

DOC-UPDATER took the subtraction option, not the corrected-figure option. I endorse that choice on the record: my second argument (wrong instrument at any value) makes the count unusable regardless of what number is put in it, so subtracting is the only remedy that actually discharges the finding. A corrected figure would have fixed the contamination and left the polarity defect standing.

(a) THE STRUCK CLAUSE IS FULLY GONE. grep over the file: "non-empty on 449" -> not present; "449 of 605" -> not present; `grep -rn "449" --include=*.md docs/` returns ZERO hits repo-wide. The clause did not survive anywhere, in any form, including as a restatement elsewhere in the block.

(b) THE REPLACEMENT CARRIES THE ASYMMETRY CLAIM ON ITS OWN. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md now reads "Where `artifacts_out` points at a real produced artefact, the summary does not duplicate it." That is the clause I told it to KEEP, promoted to sentence-initial position. Note a deliberate improvement on my own remedy text: I wrote that the sentence should begin "Where it points at a real produced artefact...", which would have left "it" with no antecedent once the preceding clause was struck. DOC-UPDATER substituted the explicit `artifacts_out`. That is the right call and I record it as a correction of my remedy, not a deviation from it. The paragraph's argument now runs: neither half of the dispatch-side defect exists here; no duplication where the field points at real work; a duplicated copy drifts, an attestation cannot. It stands without the count.

(c) THE ISS-0202 PARENTHETICAL IS SUBSTANTIVELY ACCURATE, WITH ONE INACCURACY OF GLOSS (filed as MINOR-C-3, not gating). It gives two reasons no count is quoted, and both are the reasons the gate actually found: contamination (citing ISS-0202) and wrong instrument (a presence count over all steps including gate steps that correctly produce no artefact, offered against `requirement_text == {}`'s opposite polarity). Both are accurate, and the second is the load-bearing one. Verified against the source rather than taken on trust: ISS-0202.yaml exists, was filed 2026-08-21T09:59:25Z in this run, and does measure the contamination. Checked for accuracy rather than mere presence: the parenthetical quotes NO number, so the unsound 449/605 is not smuggled back in under a citation. The one defect is the em-dash gloss, "handoffs whose `artifacts_out` names only their own file" -- ISS-0202's actual measurement is "190 of the 449 ... LIST THEIR OWN handoff file AS ONE OF THEIR OUTPUTS", a broader criterion. My own 03b measurement separates the two: 191 contain a self-reference, 115 name nothing else. So the gloss describes the 115 subpopulation while attributing it to the source that measured 190. Non-gating: no figure is quoted, the contamination claim is true under either definition, and the wrong-instrument argument is independent of both. Two-word fix. Filed.

(d) THE KEEP-CLAUSE AND THE ATTESTATION ARGUMENT ARE UNTOUCHED -- VERIFIED BY MY OWN CHECK, not by DOC-UPDATER's report. I extracted the span from "A `result.summary` is an **attestation**" to "**Legal `result.status` values" out of `git show 69fc2a1:docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` and out of the working tree, and hashed each:
    69fc2a1  sha256[:16] 23b3a6993326405a  (389 chars)
    HEAD     sha256[:16] 23b3a6993326405a  (389 chars)  IDENTICAL
The attestation argument at what were lines 288-291 is byte-identical across the rework. The KEEP clause is present. Confirmed, not taken on report.

=== (2) THE DENSITY-METRIC QUALIFICATION (my MINOR-4): PASS ===

DOES THE MARKER PREVENT THE FIGURES BEING READ AS EXACT? Yes. Three constructions do it, and the third is the one that matters:
  - "**Those density figures are directional and metric-dependent, not exact.**" -- bolded, and it denies exactness in the same words a later citer would need to contradict.
  - It defines the competing metric concretely (segments over 25 chars; digit, path-like token, or `ABC-123` identifier) and states that it reproduces the DIRECTION with different absolute values and a different least-dense file. That is a demonstration, not an assertion of uncertainty -- the reader is shown the disagreement rather than warned about it.
  - "do not cite these numbers as exact without restating the metric that produced them." This forecloses the specific misuse rather than merely disclaiming intent, which is the same construction the NOT-A-RULE framing uses and which I passed at 03b for the same reason.

IS THE REWORDED HAND-READ SENTENCE NOW TRUE? Yes. It was "a hand-read of the least-evidence-dense large summary in the corpus" -- an assertion about the corpus, which my re-measurement falsified. It now reads "a hand-read of the least-evidence-dense large summary this metric selects". "this metric" is the metric producing the 65.3%/36.7% figures the same sentence quotes, i.e. Step 1's. Under Step 1's metric the minimum IS 36.7% and IS the file Step 1 named and hand-read (handoffs/WF02-REQ027-20260816/step-02c-security-reviewer.json), which I read myself at 03b and confirmed restates its `artifacts_in` nowhere. The sentence now asserts a property of the selecting metric, and that property holds. It is TRUE, where the original was false as stated about the corpus. This is the right kind of fix: the claim was narrowed to what the evidence supports, rather than the evidence restated to fit the claim.
One observation, not a finding: the block now defines the VARIANT metric in full but still not the PRIMARY one whose numbers it quotes. That asymmetry is discharged -- the block's header points at handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json for "full figures, code and method", and the new sentence forbids citing without restating the metric. No issue filed.

=== (3) THE WF-03 STEP 5 CATCH-UP (my MINOR-2): PASS, with two MINORs attached ===

(a) KEY-PAIR COHERENCE: coherent for its purpose, with one collision recorded as MINOR-C-1. ISSUE_QUEUE.md:225-229 now names `closed_in_run:` / `closed_at:` and states why `resolved_*` is wrong for this status ("assert a resolution that a `no_defect` record explicitly did not perform"). That reasoning is right and it is the same reasoning the status itself rests on, so the vocabulary is internally consistent: `resolved` asserts removal, `instrumented` asserts shipped-but-not-fixed and carries `superseded_by:`, `no_defect` asserts checked-and-not-there and carries `closed_*`. Each terminal value's keys now assert only what that value asserts. That is the coherent construction.
   THE COLLISION, found by first-hand grep rather than reported to me: `closed_at:` is ALREADY in the corpus, once -- docs/issues/ISS-0109.yaml:314, nested under `resolution:` immediately beside `github_closed:`, and its value (2026-08-21T03:18:27Z) is the GITHUB issue's closedAt, confirmed in that record's own prose ("Closed at 2026-08-21T03:18:27Z (confirmed via `gh issue view 358 --json state,closedAt`)"). So the one existing `closed_at:` in the registry means "when GH closed", while the new rule mandates `closed_at:` for "when the run reached its verdict". One key, two meanings, in a registry ISS-0191's linter is meant to read mechanically. Non-gating -- nothing false is asserted and the scoping differs (ISS-0109's is nested under `resolution:`) -- but ISS-0200 is about to mint the precedent, so it should be disambiguated in the record it mints rather than after. See MINOR-C-1.
   Noted and NOT held against the edit: ISS-0109 is an `instrumented` record and carries `resolved_in_run:` anyway, so the corpus already uses `resolved_*` generically. The new rule deliberately corrects that. Correcting it is legitimate and I do not treat the existing usage as authority.

(b) WF-03'S DEFERENCE TO ISSUE_QUEUE.md SURVIVED: yes. The deference sentence is intact and still absolute -- "See `docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md`'s "Issue status vocabulary" for the definitions and the conditions; do not restate them here." What the new prose adds about `no_defect` (a one-line condition, plus the key names) is exactly symmetric with the treatment `instrumented` already had and that passed 03b unremarked: `instrumented` gets its condition ("shipped verified work without removing the root cause") and its required key (`superseded_by:`) named in the same sentence. `no_defect` now gets the same two things and no more -- the three-part evidence bar is NOT restated, which is the part that would have been a real duplication. Deference intact, symmetry preserved.

(c) WOULD AN AGENT FOLLOWING THE PSEUDOCODE LITERALLY NOW REACH THE RIGHT STATUS? YES -- and I tested it the way the dispatch framed it, by reading the block as a weak model executing top-to-bottom. Item 1 now reads, inside the same numbered item and before item 2: "NOT every run ends in `resolved` -- `instrumented` and `no_defect` are legal terminal values too, and each takes its own keys (a `no_defect` record uses closed_in_run:/closed_at:, never resolved_*). Check which one this run's outcome actually supports against ISSUE_QUEUE.md before writing this line." The decisive property is that this is an IMPERATIVE placed inside the executable block and explicitly ordered "before writing this line" -- not prose after the fence, where the old `instrumented` note lived and where a literal follower would never reach it before writing. A literal follower must consult ISSUE_QUEUE.md, and for THIS run Step 1 returned a reasoned NO-CHANGE verdict, so it lands on `no_defect` with `closed_in_run:`/`closed_at:`, both named right there in the block. It reaches the right status. This is the substance of the fix and it works.
   RESIDUAL, filed as MINOR-C-2 and not gating: item 1's template line still LEADS with `status: resolved, resolved_in_run:, resolved_at:` -- the wrong answer for this run, stated first and in concrete copyable form, with the correction underneath. A model that copies the first line and stops writes the false status. The imperative is sufficient to pass; a template reading `status: <resolved | instrumented | no_defect>` would remove the failure mode instead of correcting it after the fact.
   OUT OF SCOPE, recorded because Step 5 executes next -- item 2 of the same block still hardcodes the GitHub close comment as "Fixed in <run-id>." For a `no_defect` close that publishes, to an external audience, precisely the false resolution claim this status exists to prevent, and names a regression test a no-change run does not have. I am NOT gating on it: the text is pre-existing, unchanged by 291c48f, and outside the three-part scope I myself set at 03b -- gating a rework on untouched pre-existing text is the over-gating my own next_action warned against. But it is the last place the falsehood survives in the Step 5 path, and Step 5 is next. See MINOR-C-2(ii).

=== (4) ISS-0200 AC4, BYTE-IDENTITY RE-DERIVED POST-REWORK: CONFIRMED ===

My own method, re-run against merge-base 7322185 on the post-rework working tree: extract each named span by heading regex from `git show 7322185:docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` and from the working-tree file, hash with sha256. (Hashes differ from the ones I reported at 03b because I read with newline='' this time, preserving CRLF; the char counts are correspondingly +1. What is load-bearing is base-vs-head within one run of one method, and that is what is reported.)

    `git diff --numstat 7322185 HEAD -- docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` -> `80  0` (80 insertions, ZERO deletions; it was 69/0 at 03b, the +11 being this rework's net)
    `git diff -U0 7322185 HEAD` hunks: @@ -241,0 +242,65 @@, @@ -853,0 +919,6 @@, @@ -874,0 +946,9 @@
    Protected spans at HEAD: worked examples 317-390, section 4 470-852. No hunk lands inside either. DOC-UPDATER's report of the section-4 span at 470-851 is confirmed (852 is the "## 5." boundary line itself).
Section 4's validator-re-derivation requirement sits inside the byte-identical section-4 span. AC4 HOLDS post-rework. The rework clipped nothing.

=== (5) SCOPE: PASS, and the dispatch's named diff is wider than the rework ===

The dispatch named `git diff 69fc2a1 291c48f` as "the exact question". That range spans SIX commits, not one -- 574c91d, 7010717, 2733f46, bd9115a, d0e8185, then 291c48f -- so it also shows ISS-0205.yaml, both handoff JSONs, and orchestrator.log, none of which are DOC-UPDATER's rework. I isolated the rework instead: `git show --stat 291c48f` is exactly

I read all 29 added and 9 removed lines: the ISSUE_QUEUE.md key-pair clause, the HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md density qualification plus the struck-clause replacement, and the WF-03 Step 5 warning plus prose. No fourth edit, no drive-by, nothing touched in sections 2's schema fence or 4. The rest of the named range is ORCH's own gate bookkeeping and the ISS-0205 filing of my 03b MINOR-3, which I recommended -- accounted for, and correctly not DOC-UPDATER's work. issues.description: KEY-NAME COLLISION, actionable BEFORE Step 5 writes ISS-0200 rather than after. ISSUE_QUEUE.md:225-229 now mandates `closed_in_run:` / `closed_at:` as the key pair for a `no_defect` record's run-id and timestamp. But `closed_at:` already exists once in the registry with a DIFFERENT meaning: docs/issues/ISS-0109.yaml:314 carries `closed_at: "2026-08-21T03:18:27Z"` nested under `resolution:` beside `github_closed:`, and that value is the GitHub issue's closedAt, confirmed by that record's own prose ("confirmed via `gh issue view 358 --json state,closedAt`"). So one key name would carry two meanings -- "when the run reached its verdict" and "when GH closed" -- in a registry ISS-0191's linter is intended to read mechanically. Nothing false is asserted and the scoping differs (ISS-0109's is nested, the new one is presumably top-level), which is why this did not gate. But ISS-0200 is about to become the FIRST `no_defect` record and therefore the precedent every later one copies, so the disambiguation is cheapest now: either have ISS-0200 place `closed_in_run:`/`closed_at:` at top level and say in the record what they measure, or rename the pair to something that cannot be confused with a GitHub close (`verdict_in_run:`/`verdict_at:`). Also worth recording while the question is open: ISS-0109 is an `instrumented` record and carries `resolved_in_run:` anyway, so existing practice already uses `resolved_*` generically -- the new rule deliberately corrects that, and existing records may need a sweep to match it.

WF-03 STEP 5's PSEUDOCODE STILL LEADS WITH THE WRONG ANSWER, AND ITS ITEM 2 STILL PUBLISHES IT. Two parts, neither gating, both live for the Step 5 that executes next. (i) docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md item 1 still opens `status: resolved, resolved_in_run: <run-id>, resolved_at: <real UTC timestamp>` -- concrete, copyable, and wrong for this run -- with the corrective imperative underneath it. The imperative is what makes the block pass this gate (it sits inside the executable block and is explicitly ordered "before writing this line"), but a weak model that copies line one and stops still writes the false status. Removing the failure mode beats correcting it after the fact: make the template `status: <resolved | instrumented | no_defect>` and let the imperative resolve it. (ii) Item 2 of the same block hardcodes the GitHub close comment as "Fixed in <run-id>. See docs/issues/ISS-NNNN.yaml and the regression test at <test file path>." On a `no_defect` close that publishes to an external audience exactly the false resolution claim the status exists to prevent, and it names a regression test a no-change run does not have. This text is pre-existing and untouched by commit 291c48f, which is why it is outside this re-gate's scope and did not fail the edit -- but it is the LAST place the falsehood survives in the Step 5 path, and ISS-0200 is the first run that will hit it. Recommend item 2 branch on the status, or at minimum that ORCH constrain the close-comment text in this run's Step 5 dispatch.

THE ISS-0202 PARENTHETICAL MISSTATES WHAT ISS-0202 MEASURED, by one word. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's new parenthetical glosses the contamination as "ISS-0202 measured that population to be heavily self-referential -- handoffs whose `artifacts_out` names ONLY their own file". ISS-0202.yaml's actual measurement is broader: "190 of the 449 handoffs carrying a non-empty `result.artifacts_out` LIST THEIR OWN handoff file AS ONE OF THEIR OUTPUTS." These are different populations, and my own first-hand measurement at 03b separates them: 191 handoffs contain a self-reference, 115 name nothing else. The gloss therefore describes the 115 subpopulation while attributing it to the record that measured 190. Non-gating, deliberately: the parenthetical quotes no figure, so no unsound number re-enters the protocol under a citation; the contamination claim is true under either definition; and the parenthetical's second, load-bearing argument (a presence count over all steps is the wrong counterpart to `requirement_text == {}` regardless of its value) is independent of the gloss entirely. It is nonetheless an inaccurate characterisation of a cited record inside a canonical protocol document -- the same family of defect as the BLOCKER this rework just cleared -- and the fix is two words: "names their own file among its outputs".

result.next_action: PASS -- Step 3 clears outright; no further rework. Proceed to WF-03 Step 5, where ISS-0200 becomes the first record to carry `status: no_defect` and must satisfy the four-part bar in ISSUE_QUEUE.md's "Issue status vocabulary": first-hand measurement with the producing code and real figures, candidate mechanisms named individually including the ones the data did not support, stated method limitations, and the run-id/timestamp pair. All four are already available first-hand in handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json and corroborated independently in step-03b-reviewer-gate.json; the record must cite the diagnosis handoff by path and must not inherit figures from ISS-0200's own filing, which bar item 1 forbids by name. TWO OF MY THREE MINORS ARE ACTIONABLE BEFORE THAT DISPATCH, NOT AFTER: MINOR-C-1, because ISS-0200 mints the `closed_in_run:`/`closed_at:` precedent and `closed_at:` already means something else at ISS-0109.yaml:314 -- decide top-level-vs-nested placement and state in the record what the keys measure; and MINOR-C-2(ii), because WF-03 Step 5 item 2 will otherwise post "Fixed in WF03-ISS0200-20260821" plus a regression-test reference to GH#391 for a run that fixed nothing -- constrain the close-comment text in the dispatch. MINOR-C-3 (the ISS-0202 gloss) is a two-word documentation correction with no run-time consequence and can be filed for a later run. Do not reopen anything this gate or 03b certified.
